description: This topic explains the meaning and importance of transport in trade, the different modes of transport with their advantages and disadvantages, factors for choosing a mode, containerisation, and transport developments in Tanzania and East Africa.

mcq.questionText: What is the meaning of transport in commerce?

options.text: The process of advertising goods to customers
The movement of people and goods from one place to another
The storage of goods in a warehouse
The buying and selling of goods for profit

mcq.explanation: Transport is the activity of carrying people and goods from one location to another, bridging the gap between producers and consumers.

mcq.questionText: Which mode of transport is most suitable for carrying heavy and bulky goods over long distances on land?
mcq.explanation: Railway transport can carry large quantities of heavy and bulky goods over long land distances at a relatively low cost per unit.

mcq.questionText: Which mode of transport is the fastest for moving goods over very long distances?
mcq.explanation: Air transport is the quickest mode, making it ideal for urgent and perishable goods over long distances despite its high cost.

mcq.questionText: Which mode of transport is the cheapest for carrying very heavy and bulky goods over long international distances?
mcq.explanation: Water transport carries very large loads at the lowest cost per tonne, making it suitable for international bulky cargo.

mcq.questionText: Which mode of transport is mainly used to carry liquids and gases such as oil and natural gas?
mcq.explanation: Pipelines are specially designed to move liquids and gases like crude oil, petroleum and natural gas over long distances.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of road transport?

options.text: It is the cheapest for international bulky goods
It is the fastest over very long distances
It is never affected by traffic congestion

mcq.explanation: Road transport can deliver goods directly from the seller's door to the buyer's door without changing vehicles.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a disadvantage of air transport?

options.text: It is too slow for perishable goods
It is very expensive and unsuitable for heavy bulky goods
It is the cheapest mode of transport

mcq.explanation: Air transport charges high fares and has limited cargo capacity, so it is not economical for heavy or bulky goods.

mcq.questionText: Containerisation refers to the practice of:

options.text: Packing goods into large standard-sized metal boxes for transport
Storing goods inside a warehouse for a long time
Selling goods directly from containers in the market
Building new harbours along the coast

mcq.explanation: Containerisation is the use of large, standard-sized metal containers to pack goods so they can be moved easily between ships, trains and trucks.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of containerisation?

options.text: It increases the chances of goods being stolen
It makes loading and unloading slower
It reduces damage and theft of goods during transport
It requires very small handling equipment

mcq.explanation: Because goods are sealed inside strong containers, they are well protected from damage, theft and bad weather during the journey.

mcq.questionText: Which factor should a trader consider FIRST when choosing a mode of transport for fresh flowers being exported?

options.text: The speed and perishability of the goods
The name of the transport company

mcq.explanation: Fresh flowers are highly perishable, so a fast mode such as air transport is needed to deliver them before they spoil.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a major advantage of railway transport?

options.text: It offers door-to-door delivery to every home
It is suitable for transporting small parcels over short distances
It can carry large volumes of goods at low cost per unit
It does not require any fixed routes

mcq.explanation: Railways move large quantities of goods in a single train, lowering the transport cost for each unit carried.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following BEST explains the importance of transport in trade?

options.text: It creates place utility by moving goods to where they are needed
It removes the need for any advertising
It makes all goods cheaper to produce
It prevents traders from making profits

mcq.explanation: Transport creates place utility by carrying goods from areas of production to areas where they are demanded by consumers.

mcq.questionText: A disadvantage of pipeline transport is that it:

options.text: Is very expensive to construct and limited to certain products
Is the slowest way to move oil
Can easily change its route at any time

mcq.explanation: Building pipelines requires very high initial costs, and once laid they can only carry specific liquids or gases along a fixed route.

mcq.questionText: Which Tanzanian transport project is a modern high-capacity railway built to improve cargo and passenger movement?

options.text: The local bus rapid transit only
A new oil pipeline to the airport
A footpath network in rural areas

mcq.explanation: The Standard Gauge Railway is a modern railway in Tanzania built to carry larger volumes of cargo and passengers faster than the old line.

mcq.questionText: When goods must be delivered to a remote village that has no railway line or harbour, the most suitable mode of transport is usually:
mcq.explanation: Road transport is flexible and can reach interior and remote areas that other modes such as rail or water cannot serve directly.

fib.questionText: The movement of people and goods from one place to another is called _____.
fib.explanation: Transport bridges the gap between producers and consumers by moving goods and people.

fib.questionText: The mode of transport that is the fastest over long distances is _____ transport.
fib.explanation: Air transport is the quickest mode, suitable for urgent and perishable goods.

fib.questionText: The cheapest mode of transport for carrying very heavy bulky goods between countries is _____ transport.
fib.explanation: Water transport carries large loads at the lowest cost per tonne.

fib.questionText: The mode of transport used mainly to carry liquids and gases such as oil is _____ transport.
fib.explanation: Pipelines are designed to move liquids and gases over long distances.

fib.questionText: Packing goods into large standard-sized metal boxes for easy handling and transport is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Containerisation allows goods to be moved easily between ships, trains and trucks.

fib.questionText: Road transport is preferred for short journeys because it can offer _____ delivery directly from seller to buyer.
fib.explanation: Road transport delivers goods directly without changing vehicles.

fib.questionText: By moving goods to the place where they are needed, transport creates _____ utility.
fib.explanation: Place utility is created when goods are carried from areas of production to areas of demand.

fib.questionText: The modern high-capacity railway being developed in Tanzania is abbreviated as _____.
fib.explanation: SGR stands for Standard Gauge Railway, a modern railway in Tanzania.

fib.questionText: A place where ships load and unload goods and passengers is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A harbour (or port) is where ships dock to load and unload cargo, such as Dar es Salaam port.

fib.questionText: Goods such as fresh fish and flowers that decay quickly are described as _____ goods and need fast transport.
fib.explanation: Perishable goods spoil quickly, so they require fast transport such as air or refrigerated transport.

tf.questionText: Transport helps to create place utility by moving goods from where they are produced to where they are needed.
tf.explanation: Transport adds value to goods by making them available at the place where consumers demand them.

tf.questionText: Air transport is the cheapest mode of transport for carrying heavy and bulky goods.
tf.explanation: Air transport is the most expensive and is unsuitable for heavy or bulky goods.

tf.questionText: Water transport is suitable for carrying large quantities of bulky goods over long international distances at low cost.
tf.explanation: Water transport carries very large loads at the lowest cost per tonne.

tf.questionText: Pipeline transport can be used to carry solid goods such as cars and furniture.
tf.explanation: Pipelines can only carry liquids and gases like oil, petroleum and natural gas, not solid goods.

tf.questionText: Road transport is flexible and can reach remote areas that have no railway or harbour.
tf.explanation: Road transport is flexible and able to serve interior and remote locations.

tf.questionText: Containerisation increases the damage and theft of goods during transport.
tf.explanation: Containerisation reduces damage and theft because goods are sealed inside strong containers.

tf.questionText: Railway transport follows fixed routes and cannot deliver goods directly to every home.
tf.explanation: Trains run only on fixed tracks, so goods often need road transport to reach the final destination.

tf.questionText: The speed and perishability of goods is an important factor when choosing a mode of transport.
tf.explanation: Perishable goods need fast transport, so speed and the nature of the goods affect the choice of mode.

tf.questionText: The Standard Gauge Railway (SGR) in Tanzania was built to reduce the volume of goods that can be transported.
tf.explanation: The SGR was built to increase the volume of cargo and passengers carried and to make transport faster.

tf.questionText: Air transport is generally the best choice for delivering very heavy machinery within the same town.
tf.explanation: For heavy machinery over short local distances, road transport is more suitable and far cheaper than air transport.

summary.correctAnswer: The movement of people and goods from one place to another.
summary.explanation: Transport links producers and consumers by carrying goods and people.

summary.correctAnswer: It creates place utility by moving goods to where they are needed.
summary.explanation: Transport makes goods available in different markets and supports buying and selling.

summary.correctAnswer: Road, rail, water, air and pipeline.
summary.explanation: These are the five common modes used to move goods and people.

summary.correctAnswer: It provides flexible door-to-door delivery and reaches remote areas.
summary.explanation: Road transport can serve interior areas without changing vehicles.

summary.correctAnswer: It carries large volumes of heavy goods over long land distances cheaply.
summary.explanation: Railways lower the cost per unit by moving bulky goods in large quantities.

summary.correctAnswer: It is the cheapest mode for very heavy bulky goods over long distances.
summary.explanation: Ships carry large loads at low cost per tonne for international trade.

summary.correctAnswer: It is the fastest mode, ideal for urgent and perishable goods.
summary.explanation: Air transport delivers goods quickly over long distances.

summary.correctAnswer: It carries liquids and gases such as oil and natural gas.
summary.explanation: Pipelines move liquids and gases continuously over long distances.

summary.correctAnswer: Packing goods into large standard-sized metal containers for transport.
summary.explanation: It speeds up handling and protects goods from damage and theft.

summary.questionText: Factors for choosing a mode of transport
summary.correctAnswer: Cost, speed, nature of goods, distance and availability of routes.
summary.explanation: Traders compare these factors to select the most suitable and economical mode.

hoq.questionText: A Tanzanian trader must export 20 tonnes of dried cashew nuts from Dar es Salaam to a buyer in Europe at the lowest possible cost. The nuts are not perishable. Which mode of transport should the trader choose and why?

options.text: Air transport, because it is the cheapest for bulky goods
Water transport, because it carries bulky non-perishable goods over long distances at the lowest cost
Road transport, because it can drive directly across the ocean
Pipeline transport, because it carries all solid goods

hoq.explanation: Since the cashews are bulky, non-perishable and going overseas at low cost, water transport is the best choice because it offers the lowest cost per tonne over long distances.

hoq.questionText: Two traders carry the same quantity of goods on the same route, but one uses containers while the other uses loose packing. Which statement BEST explains why the trader using containers is likely to spend less time and lose fewer goods?

options.text: Containers make goods heavier so they move faster
Loose packing is always sealed against theft
Containers allow quick mechanical loading and protect goods from damage and theft
Containers remove the need for any transport vehicle

hoq.explanation: Containerisation speeds up handling using machines and seals goods inside strong boxes, reducing both time and losses from damage or theft.

hoq.questionText: A government plans to improve trade by upgrading the old railway to a Standard Gauge Railway while also maintaining roads. Why is it wise to develop both rail and road rather than rail alone?

options.text: Because roads can replace harbours for international trade
Because rail moves bulky goods cheaply between main centres while roads provide flexible door-to-door delivery to areas off the railway
Because rail and road carry exactly the same goods at the same cost
Because roads are only needed when the railway is broken

hoq.explanation: Rail and road complement each other: the railway moves large volumes cheaply between main centres, while roads extend delivery to remote areas the railway cannot reach.
